Wednesday 24 June 2026 at 19:00 UTC. Bosnia and Herzegovina and Qatar on the card. On the Qatar side, the engine's number sits +15.6pp clear of the market — one of the widest in the priced field this far out from kickoff.

On Elo, Bosnia and Herzegovina comes in 20 points ahead — Bosnia and Herzegovina at 1660, Qatar at 1640. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Bosnia and Herzegovina to win at 38%, the draw at 29%, and Qatar to win at 34%. The Desk's three-way distribution is calibrated against the W/D/L resolution Polymarket and Kalshi settle on, not against the exact scoreline. Qatar sits at 34% of the mass.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Bosnia and Herzegovina to win at 55%, the draw at 27%, and Qatar to win at 18%. The Qatar side trades at 18% on Polymarket, which prices out at American odds of +456. That's where the engine differs: our number reads 34%, +15.6pp wider.

The +3pp Pick threshold isn't on the point estimate, it's on the 5th-percentile from a 100-sample bootstrap of the Elo prior plus bonuses. On Qatar, that haircut lands the model at 29%; the market is at 18%. Even on the conservative reading, the gap is +10.7pp. We're not arguing the market is broadly wrong; the closing line and the model are in approximate agreement across recent fixtures by Brier score. The claim is narrower: this side specifically reads mispriced.

News will move the prior. With kickoff roughly 34 days out, the model is on the weekly refresh cadence; we'll move to daily once we cross the T-5d window. On a Pick this wide, it would take material news — a missing star, a tournament dropout, a venue change — to collapse the gap below the +3pp threshold; on the narrower side of the field, a single refresh can flip Pick to Pass. Either way, the Desk re-publishes after each refresh and does not recommend a trade.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Qatar a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +15.6pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: The model thinks Qatar are mispriced. Our number reads 34% on the away side; the market reads 18%. The +15.6pp gap is the Pick.
copy.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina v Qatar · the model leans Qatar
